body:
> However, that origin getter and worker global scope URL is accessed early on in the fetch for blob URLs for blob partitioning.

Can you expand on this?

From what I can tell all of the fetching should be done using _outside settings_, and never touch _inside settings_.

Ah, that comment has made me dig into our representation of outside settings representation in Ladybird, our outside settings representation seems highly likely to be incorrect 😅

However, inside settings appears to be coming from step 2. [here](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/workers.html#worker-processing-model):

> In both cases, let performFetch be the following [perform the fetch hook](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#fetching-scripts-perform-fetch) given request, [isTopLevel](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#fetching-scripts-is-top-level) and [processCustomFetchResponse](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#fetching-scripts-processcustomfetchresponse):
> 
> 1. If isTopLevel is false, [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request with [processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body) set to processCustomFetchResponse, and abort these steps.
> 2. Set request's [reserved client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-reserved-client) to inside settings.

This comes in to play in the fetch spec, where [determining the environment](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-determine-the-environment) will use reserved client as the environment when doing the blob partitioning check in the meat of fetch:

> 3. Let requestEnvironment be the result of [determining the environment](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-determine-the-environment) given request.
> 4. Let isTopLevelNavigation be true if request’s [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) is "document"; otherwise, false.
> 5. If isTopLevelNavigation is false and requestEnvironment is null, then return a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error).
> 6. Let navigationOrEnvironment be the string "navigation" if isTopLevelNavigation is true; otherwise, requestEnvironment.
> 7. Let blob be the result of [obtaining a blob object](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-url-obtain-object) given blobURLEntry and navigationOrEnvironment.

At which point we're using inside settings since reserved client is prioritized over fetch client

Got it, I see the bug now.

I think the precedent we want to look to for better layering is [navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#create-navigation-params-by-fetching). What that does is create a reserved client, which is just an environment (not yet an ESO), before every fetch in the redirect chain.

The [current worker creation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#run-a-worker) is fairly strange in that it tries to create most of the global stuff before the fetch, but then set other parts of it up after the fetch. This leads to this bug, as well as the XXX box about "This really ought to be set when the agent cluster is created, which requires a redesign of this section."

So I think the correct architecture is to only create an environment pre-fetch. Then, after the fetch succeeds, we create a full agent cluster + ESO + WorkerGlobalScope. We'd copy over the properties from the environment to the ESO, similar to step 4 of [set up a window environment settings object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#set-up-a-window-environment-settings-object).

Where this gets potentially hairy is with redirects. It would be a big pain to duplicate the logic from navigation of handling redirects manually and re-creating new clients on every redirect. Can we get away with just an initial reserved environment, and a final ESO? That would mean the environment's creation URL is incorrect during redirects. Technically that's fine, I guess, since the blob URL check only accesses the origin, and we don't allow cross-origin workers? But that's pretty fragile :(.

Sorry for the big delay, been able to spend less time browser hacking in my free time than I would like lately!

From investigating the above comment, after comparing the [window ESO setup](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#set-up-a-window-environment-settings-object) with the worker ESO steps, I just realized that step 5 of "[set up a worker environment settings object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/workers.html#set-up-a-worker-environment-settings-object)" also suffers from the same ordering issue of using global scope's URL before being set. Currently it almost reads like the intent is to set it to the pre-redirect URL, but I suppose it should probably be the post-redirect URL (and it be fixed in the same way mentioned above?).

I have also realized (hopefully not mistaken here!) that the redirect case is actually a lot less fragile than I first thought for the origin algorithm, which maybe makes this all a lot less hairy for the improved layering mentioned above. [Since redirects to data URLs are not allowed](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-http-redirect-fetch), I think pre-redirect URL is actually fine to use for the `"data"` scheme check for the ESO origin algorithm case as well, since a data scheme URL will not be changed by redirects.

Unrelated sidenote found after reading through more of the spec: I also noticed that the [constructor origin](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/workers.html#concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-constructor-origin) seems unused, likely after 5aa1a598e9ed50480436f75697b05863789e3f31
